question.text: Turnover for exchange-traded derivatives is computed as:

answer.text: Total of favourable and unfavourable differences, plus premium received on sale of options, plus differences on reverse trades
Total contract value of all trades
Gross buy value plus gross sell value

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 216 says turnover for exchange-traded derivatives is the total of favourable and unfavourable differences, plus premium received on sale of options, plus differences on reverse trades. The Trap: Turnover is not the contract value — it is the sum of the absolute P&L amounts plus option premium received plus reverse-trade differences. Note: This turnover figure is what is used to evaluate the applicability of tax-audit thresholds for derivatives trading.
